title: Dietitian visit
what: A dietitian looks at how you eat and helps build a diet that suits your health. It is a conversation and some calculations, with no procedures.
why: For overweight or underweight, diabetes, stomach, kidney, or heart conditions, pregnancy, or just to improve your diet.
duration: the first visit usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; follow-ups are shorter
tell_doctor: How your weight has changed recently
Past diets and how they went
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding

prepare.title: Food diary
prepare.text: For 3 to 7 days before the visit, write down everything you eat and drink, and when.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Bring recent blood tests, if you have them. New ones may be ordered.

prepare.title: Your goal
prepare.text: Think about what you want: lose weight, feel better, or eat right for a condition.

steps: The dietitian asks about your health, routine, and habits
Your height and weight are measured, sometimes your waist
Sometimes body composition is measured on special scales
Together you make a plan: what to change, little by little
feel: It is a regular conversation, with nothing unpleasant
Advice is usually gradual, without harsh bans
after: Change your diet gradually, as agreed
Keep up the food diary, if asked
The plan is adjusted at the follow-up

faq.q: How is a dietitian different from a nutritionist?
faq.a: Here, a dietitian is a doctor with medical training. They can work with medical conditions and order tests.

faq.q: Will I get a ready-made menu?
faq.a: Often you get a sample menu or rules. It works better when the diet fits your habits.

faq.q: Do I need to fast before the visit?
faq.a: No. If fasting blood tests are ordered, you will be told separately.

reminders.text: Dietitian visit tomorrow. Bring your food diary and test results.
